title: Retire orch-sequential, harden backend errors, remove flat collect deadline, unify kill path
goal: Fix stage timeouts silently not applying by retiring the fallback orchestrator, making backend errors fatal, replacing the 300 s flat collect deadline with the stage's declared limit, bounding always_run stages by timeout_s:, and routing all process kills through the shared kill helper.

steps.description: Run grep -rl for orch-sequential, ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT, ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT, router.timeout_s, and _orch_local_kill_slot in tests/ to enumerate every test that pins these identifiers; all matches enter the scope of the steps that change them, as required by CLAUDE.md test scope discovery.

Write failing tests: a guard that fails when the orch-sequential plugin directory exists or any file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential; a test that fails when a config naming sequential does not produce a misconfigured result; and confirm that deleting plugins/tool/orch-sequential/tests/orch-sequential-test.sh is safe by verifying its behavioral assertions are covered by other tests or are no longer required; all must redden against the current tree before any implementation.

Delete the orch-sequential plugin directory and its capabilities golden file; remove its built-in lookup entry from the orchestrator backend loader so sequential and orch-sequential are treated as unknown names like any other; delete tests that tested the orch-sequential plugin itself (plugins/tool/orch-sequential/tests/orch-sequential-test.sh); add a pool isolation assertion tagged [#1801/SPEC-11] to plugins/tool/orch-mock/tests/orch-mock-test.sh to cover the only behavioral gap not accounted for by other surviving tests; update the five SPEC-12 test files (adr059-no-tmpdir-defaults-test.sh, core-orch-run-id-isolation-test.sh, dispatch-rc-guard-test.sh, stdin-spawn-guard-test.sh, summary-mandatory-test.sh) to remove orch-sequential iterations and assertions that no longer apply; remove all remaining orch-sequential references from docs/wiki/Plugins.md, docs/wiki/plugins/orch-sequential.md, plugins/tool/orch-mock/tests/orch-mock-test.sh, plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh, tests/unit/plugin-artifact-goldens-test.sh (G5 block), tests/integration/orch-backend-misconfigured-test.sh (test commentary), and .github/issues/keepers-manifest.yaml so the guard test stays green; update potentially stale golden event-sequence files if the implementation changes event output.

Write failing tests, exercised against the installed tree (install.sh layout), that confirm a missing backend and an unreadable backend config each produce a misconfigured run result naming the backend, with no silent fallback and no discarded warning; must fail at the merge-base.

Remove both fallback paths in the orchestrator backend loader — the not-found fallback that silently selected orch-sequential, and the config-unreadable path that discarded its warning — and replace both with a hard misconfigured failure that names the backend; additionally make runner.sh check _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION immediately after sourcing contract.sh and fail the pipeline as misconfigured before dispatching any stage, so the end-to-end installed-tree test required by SPEC-4 and SPEC-10 passes.

Write failing tests that plant a hang in a run hook dispatched through each of the three orchestrator strategy types (bash-parallel map, fanout, and sequential-strategy) and confirm the stage ends timed_out naming the stage and limit, specifically by reading _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME to verify timed_out propagates and does not collapse to failed; also confirm that a stage whose timeout_s: exceeds 300 s completes without early termination; must redden on main where ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT is still passed and _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME is not propagated.

Replace the flat ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300 deadline passed to orch_collect in the map, fanout, and sequential-strategy files with a call to template_stage_time_limit so orch_collect uses the stage's declared timeout_s: (default 900 s) instead of the 300 s cap; after each collect call, read _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME and set _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME=timed_out when it is timed_out rather than mapping collect_rc=1 uniformly to failed, so the timed_out outcome propagates to the stage result; ensure orch_collect is called in the same shell context so _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME propagates back (no subshell boundary).

Write failing tests confirming that the release always_run stage is bounded by its timeout_s: value (30 s) and that the persist always_run stage is bounded by its timeout_s: value (120 s) — tested as two separate hung-stage scenarios; and that the model-call timeout field in the stage config is no longer consulted as a whole-stage deadline; must fail on main where router.timeout_s is still read for this purpose.

Remove the model-call timeout field read from the always_run dispatch path in the pipeline runner and replace the hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence there with a call to the shared process-group kill helper; move timeout_s: for release (30 s) and persist (120 s) from under the router: block to the top-level stage block in both shipped templates so template_stage_time_limit finds them; fix the template-resolver's old-shape merge path to extract and propagate always_run: from the extending template so _TPL_ALWAYS_RUN includes all declared stages (the current omission silently drops persist); also fix the hard-kill exit path so _runner_abort_trap dispatches teardown correctly; update tests/unit/exit-path-teardown-budget-guard-test.sh SPEC-1 and SPEC-3 to grep for the renamed pin variable (_SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT) instead of the old ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT name; ensure the fix does not break cleanup dispatch for prior pipeline stages (runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh pre-existing behavior) or the always-run dispatch when a hook fills its timeout.

Write a failing test confirming that when a hook spawns a child process that ignores SIGTERM, the kill path in the local engine slot terminates the child and leaves no orphan; must fail at the merge-base where the hand-rolled sequence is used.
Replace the hand-rolled TERM/0.5 s-wait/KILL sequence in the local engine slot killer with a call to the shared process-group kill helper, eliminating the second hand-rolled kill path.

Amend ADR-011 to record the orch-sequential retirement, the new default backend, and the hard-error rule for missing or unreadable backends; amend ADR-017 to record that router.timeout_s bounds only one model call; add an ## Enforced by entry to each amended statement naming the test from steps 2–11 that enforces it; remove ADR-011 and ADR-017 from config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt so npm run lint accepts them without the baseline exemption.

Fix the set -e mid-file lint violations introduced in the authored test files — orch-timeout-applies-test.sh (8 occurrences), orch-backend-misconfigured-test.sh (2 occurrences), and orch-kill-uses-pg-kill-guard-test.sh (1 occurrence) — replacing each with cmd || rc=$? so lint-test-errexit-test.sh passes.

Diagnose and fix the regression in core/pipeline/runner.sh introduced by the step-9 changes that broke the happy-path exit code across 14+ integration tests (core-pipeline-runner-test, artifact-contract-test, design-pipeline-test, always-run-exit-paths-test, runner-release-exit-paths-test, and others all showing exit 1 where 0 was expected or cleanup not dispatched); the fix must restore pre-existing runner behavior while preserving the always_run timeout_s: change.

Run npm test and npm run lint to confirm the full test suite and shellcheck pass, including all new guard tests, regression tests, and the migrated fixture tests, with no remaining references to retired identifiers outside permitted files.
